title: Penny series definition
description: Single source of truth for one data series. Everything downstream — the Postgres `series` table, TS/Zod contracts, citation rendering in apps/web — is generated from files validating against this schema. A number may only reach a page through a series id defined here (CLAUDE.md hard rule: objectivity is load-bearing).

id.description: Stable dot-namespaced id, e.g. fiscal.mts.outlays.total. Never reused; renames require an alias.

label.description: Short plain-language name shown in the UI, e.g. "Individual income taxes".

definition.description: Plain-language definition of what this series measures, in Money Stuff register. This is the text a reader sees when they click a number to find out what it is.

aliases.description: Former ids that resolve to this series.

agency.description: Source agency of record, e.g. "U.S. Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service".

dataset.description: Dataset name as published by the agency, e.g. "Monthly Treasury Statement".

dataset_url.description: Canonical URL for the dataset (the citation link).

unit.description: Unit of value_amount, as published. Conversion happens only at the presentation boundary, never in storage. `persons`/`households` are Census Bureau demographic counts (e.g. for per-capita/per-household 'for scale' figures) — never a dollar amount, and never silently divided into a usd series without the division happening at the presentation boundary, attributed as a derived per-capita/per-household figure.

magnitude.description: Scale of value_amount EXACTLY as published by the source (e.g. MTS tables report dollars in millions; Debt to the Penny reports whole dollars/cents = ones). Never converted at ingest. Mixing series of different magnitudes in a sum or chart without converting at render time is a hard-rule violation — verify this field against a live API sample before wiring ingest for a series that uses it.

accounting_concept.description: Accounting semantics. Series differing here are never summed or charted together without a declared bridge (CLAUDE.md hard rule). `projection` is a distinct concept from `deficit`/`outlay`/etc: CBO's projected figures can never be silently combined with MTS observed figures. `population` and `households` are Census Bureau demographic-count concepts, deliberately distinct from each other and from every fiscal.*/price.* concept: a person-count and a household-count are never summed together, and neither is ever summed with a dollar figure — they exist to be divided into a usd series at the presentation boundary (a per-capita or per-household figure), never combined in storage.

cadence.description: Native publication cadence of one reading. Does not by itself distinguish a monthly reading from a fiscal-year-to-date reading of the same series — that is the observation's `period_type`, not a series-level property.

citation.description: Full citation string, in the form a reader could paste into a bibliography. May contain the token {access_date}, substituted at render time.

revision_policy.description: How this source revises published values. Absent means unknown/undocumented — treat as provisional.

notes.description: Caveats a reader or an engineer needs: known category-mapping ambiguity, a magnitude that needs verifying, why this series is NOT the same concept as a similarly-named one.

not_comparable_with.description: Anti-join edges with human-readable reasons, for pairs that would otherwise look comparable (e.g. same accounting_concept) but are not. Enforced by generated incomparabilityReason() and surfaced verbatim in the UI.
